title: ROB-G clean statement: O(2^{n/2} n^2 log^2 n) work with O(n) copies, O(n) qubits and O(n^2) bits

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the ROB-G algorithm (robust shadow scores plus Grover search) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (J = max(1, n-2), r1 = 200 bitlength(16(J+1) 10^6), Q = 2^19 (n+4) copies, q = 16 angle bits, p = q + 1 + bitlength(n) phase bits, cosine table of precision 2^-22, threshold 67/400, K = floor(2^{n/2}), k_G = floor(785K/1000) Grover iterations, at most three repetitions) has worst-case total work T(N,s) = O(2^{n/2} n^2 log2^2 n) in the challenge cost model (all classical bit operations, circuit generation, gates, measurements, initialisation, table construction, address charge ceil(log2(M+2)) = O(log n) per counted operation, where M = O(n^2) is the number of allocated bits plus qubits; each source copy costs n+1; proof.md Section 7: at most 3 repetitions of at most 0.785 * 2^{n/2} Grover iterations, each with an oracle of O(Q n log n) gates, plus O(n^3 log^2 n) for acquisition and label estimation), i.e. uniform envelope B_T(n) = 2^{n/2} n^2 (log2 n)^2, whose growth index is exactly 1. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem of the fifth claim (all acquired copies independent ideal coset states), jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 49/64 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration. All constants are absolute (independent of N, s and all outcomes).

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the ROB-G algorithm (robust shadow scores plus Grover search) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (J = max(1, n-2), r1 = 200 bitlength(16(J+1) 10^6), Q = 2^19 (n+4) copies, q = 16 angle bits, p = q + 1 + bitlength(n) phase bits, cosine table of precision 2^-22, threshold 67/400, K = floor(2^{n/2}), k_G = floor(785K/1000) Grover iterations, at most three repetitions) has worst-case peak classical space S_C(N,s) = O(n^2) bits (Q records of n+p+4 bits, the 2^16-entry cosine table and its constant-size construction workspace, an O(n log log n + n)-bit label-estimation and long-division workspace, the O(n)-bit search controller (K, k_G, counters, current constants, threshold, one stored gate description); explicitly S_C <= 2^19 (n+4)(n+p+4) + 3 * 2^19 + O(n log log n + n)), i.e. envelope B_C(n) = n^2, whose growth index is exactly 0. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem of the fifth claim (all acquired copies independent ideal coset states), jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 49/64 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration. All constants are absolute (independent of N, s and all outcomes).

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the ROB-G algorithm (robust shadow scores plus Grover search) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (J = max(1, n-2), r1 = 200 bitlength(16(J+1) 10^6), Q = 2^19 (n+4) copies, q = 16 angle bits, p = q + 1 + bitlength(n) phase bits, cosine table of precision 2^-22, threshold 67/400, K = floor(2^{n/2}), k_G = floor(785K/1000) Grover iterations, at most three repetitions) has worst-case peak quantum space S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits (acquisition: one held (n+1)-qubit source copy, one test control, O(n) adder ancillas and one fair-bit qubit, released after each copy; search: n candidate qubits, O(log n) qubits for the phase accumulator, table index, table word and score accumulator, O(n) comparator and diffusion ancillas), i.e. envelope B_Q(n) = n, whose growth index is exactly 0. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem of the fifth claim (all acquired copies independent ideal coset states), jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 49/64 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration. All constants are absolute (independent of N, s and all outcomes).

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the ROB-G algorithm (robust shadow scores plus Grover search) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (J = max(1, n-2), r1 = 200 bitlength(16(J+1) 10^6), Q = 2^19 (n+4) copies, q = 16 angle bits, p = q + 1 + bitlength(n) phase bits, cosine table of precision 2^-22, threshold 67/400, K = floor(2^{n/2}), k_G = floor(785K/1000) Grover iterations, at most three repetitions) acquires exactly Q(N,s) = 2^19 (n+4) <= 5 * 2^19 n fresh source copies on every execution branch (a deterministic count; the acquisition phase is never restarted, and the search circuit is repeated at most three times on the same records, acquiring no copies; there are no aborts), so Q(N,s) = O(n), envelope B_samples(n) = n, whose growth index is exactly 0. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem of the fifth claim (all acquired copies independent ideal coset states), jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 49/64 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration. All constants are absolute (independent of N, s and all outcomes).

For the same ROB-G algorithm and configuration in proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0 for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold): at most floor(0*Q) = 0 of the Q = 2^19 (n+4) acquired copies may be malformed, i.e. the guarantee assumes that all acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states, and no adversary or corruption model is assumed for this claim. Under this promise, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 49/64 > 2/3 (proof.md Theorems 1 and 2 with no malformed copy) jointly with all four resource bounds above. No behavior is promised for malformed copies and no positive tolerance is asserted in this submission; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
